title: Fed Governor Waller Signals Openness to September Hold, Sparking Broad Stock Rally as ISM Services Beats and Yields Retreat
detail: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in remarks released the morning of September 3 that while inflation remains 'meaningfully above' the FOMC's 2% goal, recent data show signs of disinflation, and if that continues over the next two weeks of incoming data he would 'be inclined to support holding the target for the federal funds rate at its current setting' at the September 16-17 meeting. Waller argued the effects of higher tariffs have already been substantially reflected in consumer prices and that post-Mideast-war energy costs have not broadly lifted prices elsewhere, calling underlying inflation 'moderating' — a notably more dovish read than Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish August 28 Jackson Hole keynote. Markets read it as a clear dovish signal: CME FedWatch odds of a September rate hike fell roughly 12 percentage points to about 54.6% (from ~66% the day before), and the 10-year Treasury yield retreated from the week's 4.818% high (its highest since November 2023) as bonds rallied. Stocks surged on the news: the S&P 500 rose about 1.1% to roughly 7,750, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained about 1.2% to roughly 53,685, and the Nasdaq Composite jumped about 1.4% to roughly 26,584 — all three indexes' best day in weeks, snapping the prior week's rate-hike-driven slide. Same-day data added to the mixed picture: the ISM Services PMI for August came in at 55.4%, up 1.3 points from July's 54.1% and beating the roughly 54.5% forecast — the 26th straight month of services-sector expansion — while weekly initial jobless claims for the week ending August 29 rose to 206,000, a touch above the 205,000 consensus and up 2,000 from the prior week's revised 204,000, with the 4-week moving average climbing to 207,250.

title: Iran Launches Second Night of Retaliation, Striking US-Linked Bases in Kuwait and the UAE; Oil Heads for ~8% Weekly Gain
detail: Early September 3, Iran's military claimed a second consecutive night of retaliatory strikes on US-linked positions in the Gulf, following the September 1 US strikes on IRGC targets near the Strait of Hormuz and a first round of Iranian missile/drone attacks on September 2 against Camp Titin in Jordan, plus Kuwait and Bahrain. Iran's army said it hit satellite-communication systems, equipment depots, and fighter-aircraft hangars at Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait, and struck force positions and radar systems at Al Minhad Air Base in the UAE. Kuwait's air defenses engaged the incoming missiles and drones; Kuwait's foreign ministry called the strikes 'a direct threat to its security and stability' and a breach of international law. A US official said the attacks did not hit any facility where American forces are based, and no casualties or damage were confirmed by host governments; the UAE did not address the Al Minhad claim. Iran separately claimed the earlier US strikes killed 11-18 people, including a disputed strike on a wedding gathering in Sirik (4 dead, Iranian claim, unverified). The renewed multi-front escalation kept oil prices elevated, with Brent crude on track for roughly an 8% weekly gain as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remained severely disrupted.
